members.backstory: Amanda baked for a bakery that milled its own flour, dawn to dusk. She knows dough by touch — when it is alive and when it needs to rest. Amanda grew up in Duluth, cornfields, lake wind, and rust-belt factory towns. Amanda's friend Maeve owed Amanda twenty dollars since forever. members.name: Landon Braun
members.backstory: Landon ran a busy kitchen through the dinner rush for a decade. They know how to feed forty people from almost nothing and they stay calm when the fire is high. Landon grew up in Fort Wayne, cornfields, lake wind, and rust-belt factory towns. Landon's friend Carlos carried Landon home once, no questions. members.name: Dwayne Schroeder
members.backstory: Dwayne the locksmith could open anything except a conversation about fees. They have a feather touch and a shop full of key blanks older than their customers. Dwayne grew up in Peoria, cornfields, lake wind, and rust-belt factory towns. Simone, Dwayne's friend, owed Dwayne twenty dollars since forever. Dwayne learned fixing things from Simone's saying: glue it, clamp it, sleep on it, call it good.

members.name: Seamus Mazur
members.backstory: Seamus was a welder on the pipeline crews up north. They have burns in the shape of every mistake made along the way, and they do not repeat mistakes. Seamus grew up in Fort Wayne, cornfields, lake wind, and rust-belt factory towns. Rafael, Seamus's spouse, is gone — the scattering doesn't explain. members.name: Ignacio Burgos
members.backstory: Ignacio fished the coast for twenty years, longlining and running pots. He reads the water like print and he knows where the fish run when the tide turns. Ignacio grew up in Colonia del Sacramento, rolling grass, cattle, and a long brown river to the sea. Ignacio's sister Antonia had just moved to the city when the sky changed. Lucas — Ignacio's grandfather — taught Ignacio to drive on dirt roads.

members.name: Arman Banik
members.backstory: Arman was an HVAC tech — summers on rooftops, winters in crawlspaces. They have heard every noise a compressor can make, and they know what each one costs. Their parents came from Dhaka; they grew up hearing Bengali at home. Arman grew up in Pavlodar, steppe without end, apple-tree foothills, and wind with nothing to stop it. members.name: Diana Osei
members.backstory: Diana ran 911 calls for six years. She has seen people at their worst and their bravest, often in the same hour. The clearing is just another scene to work. Her parents came from Medellín; she grew up hearing Spanish at home, and still understand more than she can say. Youngest medic. Fastest hands in the village.

members.name: Sofia Chen
members.backstory: Sofia ran the community garden behind the church — forty plots, a hundred neighbors, every weed known by name. She talks to plants. The plants here listen stranger than most. Her parents came from Houston; she grew up hearing English at home, and still understand more than she can say. Knows Latin names for everything. The plants don't care.

members.name: Rafael Torres
members.backstory: Rafael was a roofer for fifteen summers in Medellín. He has never been afraid of heights, only of Mondays. His grandparents came from Brooklyn; he grew up hearing English at home. Not afraid of heights. Afraid of idle hands. He keeps a mental ledger nobody asked for. Three weeks ago Rafael took an extra strip of jerky — he remembers. He smiles when he reminds you. It's always a smile.

members.name: Miguel Santos
members.backstory: Miguel is here. His parents came from Miami; he grew up hearing English at home. Unloaded ships for twenty years. Still checks the horizon for one.

members.name: Chloe Dubois
members.backstory: Chloe interpreted at hospitals and courts — the person in the middle of every hard conversation. She speaks four languages and read faces in all of them. She learned Spanish on the job as an interpreter. She learned Arabic on the job as an interpreter. Speaks four languages. The System speaks none.

members.name: Ivy Wang
members.backstory: Ivy covered city hall for a metro daily for eight years. She knows how to get a straight answer out of someone who is paid to dodge. She learned English on the job as a journalist. Her parents came from Dhaka; she grew up hearing Bengali at home, and still understand more than she can say. Documents everything. The Codex has pictures now.

members.backstory: Henry took emergency calls for the district dispatch center, twelve-hour shifts of other people's worst days. He knows how to keep a caller breathing while the ambulance is still miles out. His grandparents came from Nashville; he grew up hearing English at home, and still understand more than he can say. Priya's deputy. They reconcile the pantry. It's intense.

members.name: Wei Chen
members.backstory: Wei kept twelve hives on the edge of town and he knows the smell of a queenright colony. He knows that cool smoke keeps a hive calm, not scared. His parents came from rural Vermont; he grew up hearing English at home, and still understand more than he can say. Keeps the hives. Says bees are better organized than people.

members.name: Vasyl Shevchenko
members.backstory: Vasyl did two tours as infantry and came home knowing how to sleep in the rain. He has carried a pack farther than anyone here will ever have to. Two tours. Doesn't talk about them. Watches the tree line.
